title: Role of Interfacial Coherency on Creep Behavior of FCC/BCC High-Entropy Alloy Multilayers.

recollection.starting_material: Equiatomic FCC/BCC high‐entropy alloy multilayers, e.g. AlCoCrFeNi (FCC) alternated with MoNbTaW (BCC)
recollection.intervention: Magnetron‐sputter deposition of multilayers with controlled bilayer period (10–100 nm) and post‐deposition annealing at 400–600 °C
recollection.structure: Coherent {111}FCC//{110}BCC interfaces for periods below ~50 nm, transitioning to semicoherent/incoherent at larger periods
recollection.mechanism: Interfacial coherency stresses impede dislocation climb and cross‐slip across the FCC/BCC boundary, providing a coherency‐strengthening effect; incoherent boundaries rely on Orowan looping
recollection.results: At 700 °C and 100 MPa, the steady‐state creep rate dropped to ~1×10⁻⁷ s⁻¹ for 20 nm periods (about an order of magnitude lower than incoherent or monolithic HEA), and time to 1% strain increased ~5×

score.note: The recollection partially captures sputter deposition and modulation-period variation, but adds nonexistent annealing and gives the wrong alloys and period range. It broadly recalls a coherent-to-less-coherent transition with increasing period, yet misses the specific M8/M16 distinction and grain-boundary-dominated M32/M80 structures. The proposed creep mechanism is substantially wrong, omitting semicoherent-interface dislocation pileup and proposed amorphization-mediated diffusion/interface slip. All testing conditions and quantitative creep results are incorrect.
